- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if price is trending down.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to inflated 30d forecasts; apply dampening factor to 3rd–5th day of forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >2.0x true value in first 5 days, reduce by 30–50% unless sentiment supports sustained high.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to overreact to recent sentiment; smooth transitions in forecast slope.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “tail inflation” — last 5–7 days often overpredict; cap forecast at 1.5x true value if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of history.
